newsitem.title: KUWAIT: U.S.-Kuwait venture gets $1.2 billion loan for complex.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-Kuwait venture gets $1.2 billion loan for complex.

text.p: Fifty-four Western, Arab and Asian banks and financial institutions Sunday agreed to lend $1.2 billion to a U.S.-Kuwaiti joint venture to build a petrochemical complex in the Gulf state.

"Today marks the end of a long financial journey," Charles Kline, president of the venture called Equate at the signing ceremony in Kuwait. "Equate should produce its first pounds of product in late July or early August 1997."

Equate, a venture between Union Carbide Corp., Kuwait's Petrochemical Industries Co. and Kuwait's Bubiyan Petrochemical Co., signed the loan agreement with a syndicate of banks assembled mainly by Kuwaiti and American financial institutions.

Bankers said the loan package was designed by Kuwait's largest commercial bank, National Bank of Kuwait, which has described the loan as the largest non-recourse financing ever arranged in the Gulf outside of the Gulf's crude oil and refinery sector.
The package is also the first major loan in the Gulf to combine conventional and Islamic financing, they said.
The total project cost is $2 billion. The non-debt portion will come from the partners' equity participation.
The interest rate is priced at 1.625 percent above London interbank offered rate or Libor if the project is completed by Sept. 30, 1998, and 1.875 percent above Libor thereafter, bankers said.
The agreement also entails a commitment fee of 0.5 percent, they said. The loan was heavily oversubscribed.
The plant, which will be one of the Gulf's largest petrochemical plants, will make 650,000 metric tons a year of ethylene, 450,000 tons a year of polyethylene and 350,000 tons a year of ethylene.

The statement said the loan was arranged by Arab Banbking Corp., Saudi-based Arab Petroleum Investments Corp., Chase Manhattan Bank, Citibank, Bahrain-based Gulf International Bank, Kuwait-based Gulf Investment Corp., JP Morgan, Kuwait Finance House.
